title: Cheshire Police facial recognition matches CCTV to Keenan Hughes; county lines dealers jailed for over five years
summary: Cheshire Constabulary's facial recognition matched CCTV of an unknown Northwich dealer to Keenan Hughes; he and Vincent Potter were stopped on 17 May 2024 with crack cocaine and jailed on 1 Jul 2024.
account: Cheshire Constabulary's release states that in April 2024 officers in Northwich learned of a phone number used by the 'Kyle' county lines gang, recovered CCTV of an unknown man suspected of using it, and submitted the image to the force facial recognition system, which returned a match to Keenan Hughes of Connah's Quay. On Friday 17 May officers on patrol spotted Hughes on Winnington Street with Vincent Potter; a search found 99 wraps of crack cocaine worth about £990 and a hunting-style knife on Hughes, and two phones, a lock knife and £960 on Potter. Both pleaded guilty and on 1 July 2024 Chester Crown Court jailed Hughes (18) for 28 months and Potter (19) for 34 months. PC Dean Butterworth said Hughes was not known locally and the technology quickly identified him as a suspect. The OECD AI Incidents Monitor records the case (2024-07-02-ee42), listing a harm type of human or fundamental rights.
purpose: Identify unknown suspects by comparing CCTV images against police custody image databases.
developer: Not named in the fetched sources
deployer: Cheshire Constabulary, Northwich Proactive Policing Unit
taxonomy_note: Public-protection policing case rather than cyber or child protection; the beneficiary is the community, the harm to the arrested is noted by OECD AIM.

ratings.reason: Two county lines dealers convicted and 99 wraps of crack cocaine and two knives taken off the street, per the force and the court outcome.

ai_role.statement: The retrospective face match supplied the suspect's identity from CCTV; the arrest arose from a later patrol sighting, and the conviction rested on seized drugs and phone messages. Sources are the deploying force's release and a local newspaper quoting the named officer; the vendor, match score and any false-match safeguards are not stated.

evidence.title: Facial recognition technology helps to identify Northwich drug dealers

evidence.title: County Lines drug dealers operating in Northwich jailed
evidence.quote: Hughes was not known in the Northwich area, but thanks to the CCTV footage and facial recognition technology, we were quickly able to identify him as a suspect.

evidence.title: Police use facial recognition AI to catch county lines drug dealers
evidence.quote: Its use directly led to the arrest and conviction of individuals involved in drug dealing, which is a harm to communities.

produced_by: A usable CCTV still of an unknown suspect
